claims.hypothesis: [C II] emission in these galaxies has an extent comparable to the optical disk
claims.experiment: uv-plane stack of the four detections fitted with a free-size exponential profile
claims.result: Exponential scale length 0.65 +/- 0.15 arcsec (~4-7 kpc), ~4 sigma significance in size
claims.finding: [C II] extent is consistent with the optical size

evidence.quote: has an average spatial extent of 4 – 7 kpc, consistent with the optical size

claims.hypothesis: [C II] luminosity is a tracer of molecular gas mass
claims.experiment: Combined the sample with literature [C II] and M_mol data and fitted L_[CII] versus M_mol
claims.result: Linear relation, slope 0.98 +/- 0.02, dispersion 0.3 dex, rho = 0.97
claims.finding: [C II] luminosity correlates with molecular gas mass with a mean absolute deviation of 0.2 dex

evidence.quote: luminosity correlates with galaxies’ molecular gas mass, with a mean absolute deviation of 0.2 dex

claims.hypothesis: alpha_[CII] is independent of depletion time, metallicity and redshift
claims.experiment: Compared alpha_[CII] medians for main-sequence, starburst, low- and high-z samples and fitted alpha_[CII] against metallicity
claims.result: Median alpha_[CII] ~ 30 Msun/Lsun; metallicity slope -0.2 +/- 0.2, consistent with zero
claims.finding: [C II] is a convenient molecular gas tracer regardless of starburst or main-sequence nature and for metal-poor galaxies

evidence.quote: is largely independent of galaxies’ depletion time, metallicity, and redshift

claims.hypothesis: alpha_[CII] stays constant even for the most extreme starbursts
claims.experiment: Estimated gas masses for local (U)LIRGs from depletion-time models and compared alpha_[CII]
claims.result: alpha_[CII] decreases by 0.3 dex for the most extreme starbursts with the averaged-model gas masses but stays constant with the Scoville2017 model only
claims.finding: More observations are needed to explore the extreme starburst regime

evidence.loc: 3.2 [C II] as a tracer of molecular gas
evidence.quote: More future observations will be needed to explore in a more robust way the most extreme starburst regime.

why_this_data.value: Band 9 [C II] observations of the largest sample at this redshift; ALMA Band 7 added for dust masses

evidence.quote: Currently this is the largest sample of galaxies observed with ALMA at this redshift

why_this_method.value: Sources are resolved, so fluxes are measured in the uv plane with extended models

evidence.quote: We concluded that, when fitting the sources in the *uv* plane, we could measure their correct total fluxes

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: PSF model for total fluxes rejected because it underestimates fluxes of extended sources

evidence.quote: whereas by using a PSF model instead we would have underestimated the fluxes

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gaussian profile instead of exponential gives consistent [C II] fluxes

evidence.quote: fitting the data with a Gaussian profile instead of an exponential would give consistent

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Dust-based gas masses not adopted; Schmidt-Kennicutt masses used as more robust for galaxies without 850 um detections

evidence.quote: In the following we use the $M_{\mathrm{mol}}$ obtained from the Schmit-Kennicutt relation

limitations_admitted.value: Fluxes depend critically on the assumed model size taken from optical images

evidence.quote: However, the returned fluxes critically depend on the model size that we used and that we determined from the optical images.

limitations_admitted.value: Source size cannot be constrained from individual sources because of low S/N

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the size of the emission cannot be constrained from the data on individual sources, given the limited S/N ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: Observed in a more extended configuration than requested, giving 5-10 times higher flux errors

evidence.quote: Our sources were therefore resolved.
we obtained a flux measurement error 5 – 10 times higher than expected

referee_caveats_inferred: Total [C II] fluxes rest on optical-size exponential models; a different size changes flux linearly, so L_[CII] and alpha_[CII] are model dependent
Detections at 2.3 sigma are called real from a posteriori reasoning; small numbers (4 secure, 2 tentative)
Stack excludes three non-detections (incl. an AGN and two poor-weather sources), which may bias the average ratio high
alpha_[CII] derived from heterogeneous literature gas masses (different alpha_CO, SK relation, depletion-time models) that partly share assumptions with the SFR used in L_IR
Single Cycle 1 execution; no flux calibrator or calibration uncertainty stated for Band 9

missing_for_reproduction: CASA/pipeline versions, calibrators and flux scale uncertainty
Exact channel ranges, GILDAS fit settings and HST-derived sizes/positions per galaxy (only R_e listed)
HST, Spitzer and Herschel inputs and SED-fit settings needed to reproduce L_IR and M_dust
Full literature compilation table (stated to be online)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 10-50 GB raw for 10 Band 9 fields plus Band 7 (inferred; two Cycle 1 observing nights)
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA data and main procedure are described and the GILDAS uv-fitting approach is documented, but calibration details, per-source fit inputs and the literature compilation are incomplete.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state that the data are public, and key inputs (HST-derived sizes, SED-based L_IR, full literature table, channel ranges) are not fully given.
